content:
maya: Quick follow-up from the RFC  we need a concrete onboarding playbook for customer VPCs into the private control plane. Sketching a short runbook for peering/privatelink, handshake, failover, and cert propagation. PTAL.

charlie: SGTM. can you paste the runbook steps here? we should include circuit-breakers for bad egress routes.

maya: Ran a quick draft: 
```
Runbook: private VPC onboarding (high level)

0) Prechecks
  - confirm customer VPC CIDR(s) (no unexpected overlap)
  - confirm route tables, IGW/NAT presence and egress pattern
  - get security & network approvals

1) Create connectivity
  - prefer Privatelink for overlapping CIDRs or orgs with strict routing
  - otherwise create VPC Peering and update routes

2) Handshake/token exchange
  - customer creates an IAM role or cross-account role
  - we STS assume role and exchange a short-lived bootstrap token
  - tokenize handshake with nonce + TTL

3) Bootstrap agent
  - agent downloads pinned CA bundle and bootstrap token
  - agent registers and reports /healthz

4) Validation
  - curl https://private-cp.example.com/healthz --cert <agent-cert>
  - verify controlplane metrics: handshake latency, packet loss

5) Route announcement & egress test
  - route test traffic through data path
  - ensure stable egress IPs if customer needs whitelisting

6) Monitoring & rollback
  - enable logs, trace sampling, and alerts
  - circuit-breaker: degrade to hosted API on >5% error or latency spikes
```

charlie: Nice. include example commands for the token exchange and the simple health check so SREs can run it without hunting docs.

maya: Example snippet: 
```
# assume role and get token
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedwoodOnboardRole --role-session-name onboard-123

# curl health check (mTLS)
curl --cert client.pem --key client.key https://private-cp.example.com/healthz
```

izzy: Suggestion: always prefer Privatelink for orgs with overlapping CIDRs. For peering we need explicit SNAT when the customer's chosen subnet overlaps our internal mesh addresses  call this out.

sam: Question: ephemeral egress IPs  if we peer + SNAT, who owns the SNAT IP? We should avoid IP churn for customers who whitelist our egress.

maya: Proposal: allocate a stable egress pool. For peered setups we can offer an optional per-customer NAT gateway in our account that provides stable egress IP(s). For Privatelink, encourage customers to use their NLB or an egress appliance they control.

charlie: Concern: per-customer NAT gateways add cost and permissions. Alternative is a shared egress fleet with per-customer source NAT using port-preserving SNAT, but that complicates traceability and SLA boundaries. Need cost + security tradeoff documented.

izzy: Also add cert rotation details: CA rotation flow should use a "dual trust" window on agents  push new CA as secondary, rotate connectors, then remove old CA after TTL. Agents must accept bundles with two CAs during transition.

maya: Added rotation steps to the runbook: 1) push new CA as secondary, 2) schedule connector roll, 3) monitor auth errors, 4) retire old CA after 24h window. Will include TTLs and explicit rollback instructions (rollback token + pinned-CA restore).

deploy-bot: deploy/handshake-bundle v1.3.0 deployed to staging at 2024-11-15T10:12Z :rocket:

sam: One more security note: health-check endpoints should be authenticated (short-lived mTLS or bearer token) to avoid abuse from on-prem scanners. Also rate-limit those checks.

charlie: Operational circuit-breaker defaults we should add to playbook: if >5% packet loss over 1 minute or controlplane RTT > 500ms, automatically failover to hosted API path and open a paging alert to oncall. Document SLOs and the fallback path semantics.

maya: I'll update the RFC + runbook with these items and create a short onboarding checklist doc (prechecks, roles, expected costs, rollback). Who wants to own the NAT-cost mitigation plan? @sam?

sam: I can own it. I'll build a cost model and propose a pooled-NAT vs per-customer NAT comparison next week.

izzy: :thumbsup: I'll add an e2e test in the onboarding harness that simulates overlapping CIDRs and ensures Privatelink chosen path and cert rotation works.

charlie: thanks  once Maya pushes the updated runbook let's schedule a quick RFC follow-up meeting to lock the defaults and the rollback play.

maya: Will do. I'll push the doc and ping in #architecture when it's live.
